chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May I be your ransom, I had a fat ram for sacrificing (as Udhiyah). When I took it and laid it down, it looked at me, so I felt mercy for it and was softened towards it. Then I slaughtered it.' He said to me, 'I did not like for you to do that. Do not raise (a beast) from these and then slaughter it.'

key_terms.أُضَحِّيَ: To offer a sacrifice (Udhiyah) during Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette regarding raising animals for sacrifice in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against raising livestock specifically for sacrifice, noting that the animal's gaze can evoke mercy in the sacrificer, potentially causing hesitation or a lack of decisiveness (*ghadrah*) in the act. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the spiritual state of the sacrificer, ensuring the act is performed with purpose rather than mere sentimentality. The ruling underscores that while mercy is virtuous, excessive attachment prior to slaughter may detract from the solemnity of the ritual.
